answers.text: I've spent six years as a software engineer, the last three at a payments company in Bengaluru. My biggest piece of work was splitting our settlement service out of the monolith into three services. I wrote the design document, got sign-off from two other teams and ran the cut-over over four weekends. On-call pages dropped from roughly 30 a month to 8. I'm applying now because the decisions I find most interesting, such as what to build and for which merchants, are made one level above me, and I want the business training to make them well.

I can't share the transaction volumes or revenue numbers; they're confidential to the company. What I can say is that settlement runs every night for all of our merchants, so an outage there is visible to customers the next morning.
Actually, I managed the whole team for that migration. Well, not formally. There were three of us and I was the one who wrote the plan, but I didn't have anyone reporting to me.
By the way, do you know whether the ISB hostel allows cooking? I'm vegetarian and I was wondering about the mess food.
